title: CLI errors print to stdout instead of stderr, defeating shell 2>/dev/null guards

description:
WHAT: Every error from the main CLI dispatch path is written to stdout via print!, not stderr. Confirmed empirically: `story move SH-41 done x --quiet >out 2>err` yields 54 bytes on stdout and 0 bytes on stderr (exit 2).

WHERE: src/main.rs lines 28, 68, and 81 all call print!("{}", output::render_error(...)). Only the TUI path (main.rs:13,17) and the web --serve path (main.rs:44,49) correctly use eprintln!.

WHEN / LAST KNOWN GOOD: none — present since aee7bac (2026-03-11, 'feat: add core story cli workflow'). This is a day-one defect, not a regression.

EXTENT (why it matters):
1. Callers cannot suppress errors with 2>/dev/null. The storyhook-managed post-merge hook does exactly this: `story move $ID done ... --quiet 2>/dev/null || true`. Because the error lands on stdout, it leaks into unrelated output — observed during a routine fast-forward of main, which printed 'error: story SH-41 is closed and cannot be modified' in the middle of the merge diffstat.
2. With --json, error payloads are interleaved into the stdout data stream that scripts parse as results.
3. Violates the POSIX convention that diagnostics go to stderr and results to stdout, which every piping/scripting consumer assumes.

REPRO:
  story move <any-closed-id> done "probe" --quiet >/tmp/out 2>/tmp/err; echo "exit=$?"
  wc -c </tmp/out   # 54 — should be 0
  wc -c </tmp/err   # 0  — should be 54

FIX SKETCH: change the three print! calls to eprint! . Note render_error already returns a trailing newline, so eprint! (not eprintln!) preserves current formatting.

REGRESSION TEST: assert an erroring invocation writes an empty stdout and a non-empty stderr, for both plain and --json modes.
